bug_report_content:
id: 86
status: Fixed
summary: @inheritDoc doesn't play well with interfaces
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 1
commentCount: 7
Comment 0 (2010-01-04): If I use interface inheritance with @inheritDoc, the compiler doesn't know about the types used in the method signature. Sample code: /** * Interface * @interface */ A = function() {}; /** * @param {string} a */ A.prototype.foo = function(a) {}; /** * @constructor * @implements {A} */ B = function() {}; /** * @inheritDoc */ B.prototype.foo = function(a) { alert(a.substring(0)); // ERROR - could not determine the type of this expression };
Comment 1 (2010-01-04): I should add, this only shows up with --report_unknown_types turned on.
Comment 3 (2010-01-08): should be fixed at head
Comment 4 (2013-03-21): Are you sure this is fixed? I just tried this on http://closure-compiler.appspot.com/ and it didn't produce any warnings /** @interface */ A = function() {}; /** @param {string} a */ A.prototype.foo = function( a) {}; /** * @constructor * @implements {A} */ B = function() {}; /** @inheritDoc */ B.prototype.foo = function( a) { alert(a.substring(0)); }; var inst = new B(); inst.foo(1); But this _does_ produce warnings /** @interface */ A = function() {}; /** @param {string} a */ A.prototype.foo = function( a) {}; /** * @constructor * @implements {A} */ B = function() {}; /** @param {string} a */ B.prototype.foo = function( a) { alert(a.substring(0)); }; var inst = new B(); inst.foo(1);
Comment 5 (2015-07-30): This is not fixed. Nicolas, could you reopen the bug?
Comment 6 (2015-07-30): If you think this is not fixed, please re-open a bug on github with a repro case. The example here works if you declare A and B rather than leave them as global variables. (You can try it on appspot.) /** @interface */ var A = function() {}; /** @param {string} a */ A.prototype.foo = function( a) {}; /** * @constructor * @implements {A} */ var B = function() {}; /** @inheritDoc */ B.prototype.foo = function( a) { alert(a.substring(0)); }; var inst = new B(); inst.foo(1); The varcheck pass of the compiler, which runs before type checking, warns about global variables in the code.
